newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: HSBC says Australian wages rise in April.
newsitem.headline: HSBC says Australian wages rise in April.

text.p: Average wage increases achieved under the federal enterprise bargaining system rose 4.7 percent in the month of April compared with 4.0 percent in the March quarter but this should not overly concern the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), the HSBC Markets Wages Report said.

"If he is pondering another rate cut, RBA Governor Ian Macfarlane will not be unduly discouraged by wages increases in major agreements reached in April," HSBC chief economist John Edwards said of the investment bank's analysis of wage deals.
While the average increase per employee was markedly higher than in the 1997 first quarter, six of the eight major agreements concluded in the month were in the public sector, he said.
"It is a small sample, and influenced by the fact that some of the local government staff receiving most of the increases have hitherto received little more than national minimum award increases."

He said the eight agreements covered about 13,000 employees, with private sector deals struck by Qantas and the Royal Automobile Club of Queensland which awarded rises of 4.0 percent and 3.2 percent, respectively.

HSBC said official wages data showing annual growth of 4.3 percent to February 1997 was uncomfortably close to the RBA's 4.5 percent ceiling, but even so, this had not stopped the central bank from easing monetary policy by 50 basis points on May 23.
The May 23 rate cut was the fourth cut in the official cash rate since July last year.
"This suggests that the bank's private view on wages is more sanguine than their repeated public warnings would have us believe," HSBC said.
